sections.h2: How does selling a house in Muskegon, MI work?
sections.html:
A Muskegon seller lists, sells privately or takes a cash purchase, then records the deed at the county Register of Deeds and settles the property tax. If the house has been a rental, the city's registration and inspection rules add steps that a buyer will ask about.

The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate puts Muskegon at 37,224 residents, level with its 2020 base. The city has 53.1% owner-occupancy across 13,996 households, a median owner-occupied value of $142,300 and a median gross rent of $996. Median household income is $44,735 and 24.9% of residents live in poverty. In a city with those figures, a repair bill of a few thousand dollars is a large share of the sale price.

About 22% of residents are under 18, 14.8% are 65 or older, and 15.5% of adults hold a bachelor's degree. The mean commute is 20.6 minutes, and 81.4% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most households are settled rather than moving through. Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $1,064, close to the $996 median gross rent.

sections.h2: What is Muskegon like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Muskegon is a Lake Michigan harbor city and the Muskegon County seat, sitting on the south shore of Muskegon Lake. It covers 18.20 square miles, and 22.3% of that is water.

The Muskegon River empties into the lake at the northeast end, and the city borders North Muskegon, Muskegon Township, Fruitport Township, Muskegon Heights, Roosevelt Park and Norton Shores. Grand Rapids is 42 miles southeast. Settlement took off in 1837 with the lumber trade, which earned the city nicknames like Lumber Queen of the World, and Bluffton was annexed in 1889.

  • Downtown: a stretch of about two miles along the lake, with hotels, a convention center finished in 2021 and the Trinity Health Arena.
  • Schools: Muskegon Public Schools has served the city since 1860, and Muskegon Community College and Baker College are local.
  • Getting around: I-96, US 31, M-46 and M-120 serve the city, the MATS bus system runs routes and trolleys, and the Lake Express car ferry crosses to Milwaukee.
  • Air: Muskegon County Airport has nonstop flights to Chicago O'Hare.

Winter is a factor in condition. Muskegon averages 87.2 inches of snow a year, mostly lake-effect, with 48 snowy days, and January alone brings about 29 inches. Roofs, gutters and furnaces take the brunt, so a buyer's inspector will look at them first.

sections.h2: What rental rules affect a Muskegon house before I sell?
sections.html:
Every rental unit in the city must be registered and inspected, and the certificate does not pass to a new owner. A buyer who plans to rent the house starts the process over with a new certificate and a passed inspection.

The first inspection earns a 6-year certificate when no violations turn up, and a 3-year cycle when violations are found. The city follows the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code, so rental dwellings need carbon monoxide readers, and a new certificate requires a licensed contractor to verify the furnace and water heater at 0 ppm in the breathable area. Owners living more than 30 miles away must name a responsible party within a 30-mile radius.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Muskegon short-term rental with its license?
sections.html:
Mostly no. Short-term rental licenses issued after the ordinance was adopted are non-transferable, and the registration belongs to the owner who obtained it.

The one exception covers properties that held an active short-term rental status before March 2024, which can make a one-time status transfer in any zone with a signed formal document. The new owner still completes registration and inspections. The city's overlay district splits short-term rentals into 11 zones with caps that range from 13 in Zone 11 to 95 in Zone 9, and Zone 1, Beachwood and Bluffton, has a waitlist. Properties inside the downtown authority, the Lakeside Business Improvement District and the Lakeside Corridor Improvement Authority are exempt from the caps.

Registration for a single-family short-term rental is $500 a year, rising by $500 for each added unit. Tell any buyer whose offer depends on short-term rental income to read the overlay rules first.

sections.h2: When are Muskegon property taxes due?
sections.html:
Summer taxes are billed July 1 and due by September 14, and winter taxes are billed December 1 and due by February 14. Unpaid summer tax collects interest at 1% per month after the due date, plus a 3% penalty if still unpaid by February 14.

A 3% penalty is added to winter taxes after the due date. Anything the city has not collected by February 28 moves to the County Treasurer as delinquent on March 1, and the county collects it from there. Ask your title company how it will prorate the current bill at closing.

Under MCL 211.27a the taxable value uncaps the year after the transfer, and the buyer's bill follows the state equalized value. A seller who claimed the principal residence exemption has 90 days from moving out to rescind it under MCL 211.7cc, with a $5 per day penalty, capped at $200, for a late filing.

sections.h2: What does the Muskegon County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
Recording a deed, mortgage or other instrument in Muskegon County costs $30 per document no matter how many pages it has.

  • A warranty deed, land contract or assignment of land contract with a warranty clause needs a $5 tax certificate from the County Treasurer's Office before recording.
  • Copies of real estate records are $1 per page, and certification is $5 per document.
  • State transfer tax is $3.75 and county tax is 55 cents per $500 of value, so a $150,000 sale carries 300 units at $4.30, or $1,290.
  • The county offers a free Fraud Guard alert that emails you when your name appears on a recorded document.

Transfers between a parent and child, or a grandparent and grandchild, are exempt from the state tax under MCL 207.526.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Muskegon house fast?
sections.html:
Three routes are open: list it, sell it yourself, or sell to a cash buyer. Weigh repair costs, carrying costs and timing against the price, since a cheaper house can lose a larger share of its value to fixes.

Whichever you choose, gather these before you talk to buyers:

  • Your rental certificate and the last furnace and water heater inspection, if the house was rented.
  • Recent summer and winter tax bills, so the title company can settle the balance.
  • Records of roof, gutter and basement repairs after a lake-effect winter.
  • Your deed or land contract paperwork.

If you would like a Muskegon cash offer, send the address and the condition of the house. We buy as-is, so a failed rental inspection or a winter-damaged roof does not have to be fixed first.

faqs.q: Does a Muskegon rental certificate transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Certificates do not transfer to new owners, so the buyer must open a new certificate and pass inspections.

faqs.q: How long is a Muskegon rental certificate valid?
faqs.a: Six years if the first inspection finds no violations, and three years if violations are found. The yearly registration fee keeps the certificate in good standing between inspections.

faqs.q: When do delinquent Muskegon property taxes go to the county?
faqs.a: March 1. The city turns over anything it has not collected by February 28, and the County Treasurer collects it from that point.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a $150,000 Muskegon sale?
faqs.a: $1,290. That is $1,125 at the state rate of $3.75 per $500 plus $165 at the county rate of 55 cents per $500.

faqs.q: What does Muskegon charge to register a short-term rental?
faqs.a: $500 a year for a single-family unit, rising to $1,000 for a duplex and $2,500 for a quinplex. Re-inspections cost $100 for the first and climb in $100 steps.
